questions.q: Training loss keeps falling while validation loss rises and the gap widens. What does this pattern suggest?
options: Overfitting (though the curves alone do not prove the cause)
The model has not started learning yet
The learning rate is too small
questions.explain: A widening generalization gap (validation − training) is the classic overfitting signature. Underfitting looks different: both losses stay high and close together.

questions.q: With Model Capacity set to 2, both losses stay high and close together. What is this?
options: Underfitting: the model is not flexible enough to fit even the training data
questions.explain: A small gap with high losses means the model cannot capture the pattern at all. More capacity (or features) would help here, not regularization.

questions.q: Validation losses for epochs 1–7 are $1.0,\ 0.8,\ 0.7,\ 0.72,\ 0.71,\ 0.75,\ 0.8$. With early-stopping **patience 3**, when does training stop and which weights are restored?
questions.explain: The best validation loss is $0.7$ at epoch 3. Epochs 4, 5, 6 do not beat it, and at epoch 6 we have $6 - 3 = 3 \ge$ patience, so training stops and the best weights (epoch 3) are restored. $0.71$ at epoch 5 is not an improvement over $0.7$.

questions.q: Why can't a real training run simply use the 'hindsight minimum' (lowest validation loss over all 100 epochs)?
options: It is always worse than the online early-stopping epoch
It requires knowing future validation losses, which are not available while training
It only exists for underfitting models
questions.explain: Online early stopping only uses validation results observed so far. The hindsight minimum is shown just for comparison; with noisy curves and small patience the online rule may stop earlier or later.
